A 2007 evaluation of three brands of professional nursing shoes found that the shoe with a more cushioned insole and better arch support reduced lower-extremity muscle effort compared to the other two, but the study was small and brand-specific.

What the research does support more broadly is that footwear comfort matters. In a survey of 125 nurses across emergency and outpatient departments, 72% of nurses reporting low footwear comfort also reported foot and heel pain, compared with 28% of those reporting high footwear comfort. The 2023 heel pain guideline grades orthotics on their own B-against for short-term plantar fasciitis relief, meaning evidence leans against using them as a standalone option.

A practical approach: choose a shoe that fits well, has some cushioning and does not pinch the toes. If you already have heel or arch pain, the exercises on this page target the tissues directly. Shoes and inserts can help with comfort during a shift, but they do not replace the stretching and strength work.

Source: Koc TA Jr, Bise CG, Neville C, et al. Heel Pain - Plantar Fasciitis: Revision 2023. Journal of Orthopaedic & Sports Physical Therapy. 2023;53(12):CPG1–CPG39.

### Do compression stockings help nurses with foot and leg pain?

Compression stockings have one of the better-controlled studies behind them for standing-related discomfort. In a randomized trial of 40 security guards standing roughly 12-hour shifts, both the 15-20 mmHg and the 20-30 mmHg compression-stocking groups avoided the significant rise in foot and leg discomfort, fatigue and swelling seen in the group that wore regular socks. Participants commonly said the lower-pressure stocking was easier to put on.

A pilot randomized trial of 20 nursing students compared knee-length and thigh-length compression stockings worn during 9-hour clinical training shifts. Both groups reported high satisfaction, though the sample was too small to show clear differences in outcomes between the two lengths.

The Garcia trial was all male security guards, not nurses, and neither study was large. But compression stockings are one of the few standing-specific interventions with randomized evidence behind them. A 2015 occupational health review lists them alongside floor mats and supportive footwear as interventions with some evidence for reducing discomfort during prolonged standing work. They do not replace stretching or strength work. They manage the swelling and fatigue, while the calf and fascia still need their own attention.

Source: Garcia MG, Roman MG, Davila A, Martin BJ. Comparison of physiological effects induced by two compression stockings and regular socks during prolonged standing work. Human Factors. 2023;65(4):562–574.
Source: Waters TR, Dick RB. Evidence of health risks associated with prolonged standing at work and intervention effectiveness. Rehabilitation Nursing. 2015;40(3):148–165.

### What can you do before and after a shift in 3, 5, or 10 minutes?

If you have 3 minutes: do the two calf stretches (straight knee and bent knee, 30 seconds each side). That covers the single strongest modifiable risk factor, a tight calf, and takes the same time as tying your shoes.

If you have 5 minutes: add the plantar fascia stretch (30 seconds each foot). This is the combination the 2023 guideline grades A for plantar fasciitis. If your heel is worst on the first steps of the day, do the fascia stretch before your feet touch the floor.

If you have 10 minutes: add the heel raises (3 sets of 10) and the short foot (3 sets of 10 with a 5-second hold). This covers the strength side, graded B in the guideline. On off days, 10 minutes covers everything on this page.

Consistency matters more than length. Three minutes of calf stretching every shift day, done at the same point in your routine, is more useful than a longer session you skip when the schedule changes.

Source: Koc TA Jr, Bise CG, Neville C, et al. Heel Pain - Plantar Fasciitis: Revision 2023. Journal of Orthopaedic & Sports Physical Therapy. 2023;53(12):CPG1–CPG39.
Source: Riddle DL, Pulisic M, Pidcoe P, Johnson RE. Risk factors for plantar fasciitis: a matched case-control study. Journal of Bone and Joint Surgery (American). 2003;85(5):872–877.

### Could foot pain from a nursing shift be plantar fasciitis or something else?

General ache and tiredness from a long shift is common and usually goes away with rest. Plantar fasciitis is a specific condition: sharp pain near the heel, worst on the first steps after rest (getting out of bed, standing after a long sit). If your pain follows that pattern, the exercises in [plantar fasciitis exercises and stretches](https://walkito.site/plantar-fasciitis-exercises/) are the fuller guide, and the calf raise detail is in [calf raises for plantar fasciitis](https://walkito.site/calf-raises-plantar-fasciitis/).

If your arches feel flat or rolled in by the end of a shift, the arch exercises in [flat feet exercises for fallen arches](https://walkito.site/flat-feet-exercises/) target the muscles that hold the arch up. Pain along the shin could be shin splints. Pain in the Achilles tendon at the back of the heel is a different problem.

If pain from standing is your main question and you are not a nurse, [why do my feet hurt after standing all day](https://walkito.site/feet-hurt-standing-all-day/) covers the same exercises with a broader audience. For the standing-desk version of this problem, see [standing desk foot pain](https://walkito.site/standing-desk-foot-pain/). If you are not sure what is causing the pain, see a clinician before loading it with exercise.

### See a clinician first if

- the pain followed a specific injury or fall at work
- you cannot put weight on the foot, or you are limping
- the foot is numb, tingling, burning, swollen or warm
- the heel or foot is red, or you have a fever or feel unwell
- pain wakes you at night
- pain is sharp, or getting worse despite easing the load
- pain is in one pinpoint spot and gets worse with activity, which can be a stress fracture pattern and not standing fatigue
- one leg or foot has swollen suddenly and is painful, red or warm
- you have diabetes, reduced feeling in your feet or poor circulation
- the pain has not eased after several weeks of lighter shifts, better shoes and the exercises on this page

### Doing it as a plan

You do not have to work out the order, the doses or when to move to a harder version. Walkito builds a plan one week at a time around one goal. If your foot pain follows the morning-pain pattern of plantar fasciitis, the first goal is morning pain at 1 out of 10 or less for 14 days in a row.

#### How many steps do nurses walk in a 12-hour shift?

In a tracker-based study of Korean hospital nurses, the average was about 9,360 steps per shift, covering roughly 5.8 km over 9.4 hours. That is well above the average daily step count for the general adult population, and the sustained walking on hard floors is a major contributor to foot pain in nursing.

#### Are 12-hour shifts worse for foot pain than 8-hour shifts?

In a survey of paediatric hospital nurses, working 12-hour shifts in the intensive care unit was the single work factor that independently raised the odds of disabling foot and ankle problems. The total load on the foot increases with shift length, and recovery time between shifts is shorter when the shifts themselves are longer. That said, the type of work and the floor surface matter too, not just the hours.

#### Should nurses wear clogs or sneakers for foot pain?

There is no large trial comparing nursing clogs to sneakers for foot outcomes. What the evidence does support is that footwear comfort is strongly associated with foot pain: in one survey, 72% of nurses reporting low footwear comfort also reported foot and heel pain. Choose a shoe that fits well, has some cushioning and does not pinch the toes. Shoes alone do not replace the stretching and strength work on this page.

#### Do compression socks help nurses on long shifts?

In a randomized trial of 40 security guards standing 12-hour shifts, both 15-20 mmHg and 20-30 mmHg compression stockings prevented the rise in discomfort and swelling seen with regular socks. The trial was not in nurses specifically, but the mechanism is the same: compression helps blood return from the lower legs during long periods on your feet. Most participants found the lower-pressure stocking easier to put on.

#### Is foot pain from nursing something you just have to live with?

Foot pain from standing and walking is common in nursing, but "common" does not mean inevitable. The 2023 heel pain guideline grades calf and fascia stretching A and strength training B. Compression stockings have randomized evidence behind them for standing-related discomfort. A few minutes of calf stretching before or after each shift, combined with strength work on off days, targets the tissues that take the most strain.

#### Can plantar fasciitis develop from nursing work?

Standing for most of the working day raised the odds of plantar fasciitis 3.6 times in a matched case-control study of 50 cases and 100 controls. Reduced ankle flexibility raised them 23.3 times. Nurses face both risk factors, prolonged standing and limited break time to stretch, which is why the exercises on this page overlap heavily with those in the plantar fasciitis guide.

#### What is the single best thing a nurse can do first for foot pain?

Among the options reviewed on this page, daily calf stretching has the strongest guideline backing (grade A for plantar fasciitis) and targets the single strongest modifiable risk factor, a tight calf. It takes about 2 minutes, needs no equipment and can be done in the break room or at home. Adding compression stockings on shift days covers the swelling and fatigue side.

## Standing desk foot pain: why it happens and what helps

Language: English · https://walkito.site/standing-desk-foot-pain/ · published 2026-10-04 · updated 2026-10-04

Switching to a standing desk is supposed to be better for you, but your feet and legs may disagree in the first few weeks. Foot pain from a standing desk usually comes from standing too long in one position, not from the desk itself. The research points to shorter standing bouts, a mat, the right shoes and a few exercises you can do without leaving your desk.

- A 2017 systematic review of 25 laboratory studies found that clinically relevant musculoskeletal symptoms developed after about 40 minutes of uninterrupted standing, shortened to 42 minutes in people prone to back pain. The authors recommended not standing continuously for more than 40 minutes (Coenen and colleagues, 2017).
- A 2015 expert statement commissioned by Public Health England recommends initially accumulating 2 hours per day of standing and light activity during work, eventually progressing to 4 hours per day, broken into shorter bouts (Buckley and colleagues, 2015).
- A 2014 systematic review of 14 studies found sufficient evidence that sit-stand workstations reduce low-back discomfort, with no decrease in productivity, but found no optimal sit-stand time ratio (Karakolis and Callaghan, 2014).
- A 2015 review of occupational health research found prolonged standing associated with musculoskeletal discomfort, fatigue and leg pain, and listed floor mats, compression stockings and supportive footwear among the interventions with evidence behind them (Waters and Dick, 2015).
- Reduced ankle flexibility, meaning a tight calf, was the strongest predictor of plantar fasciitis in a 2003 case-control study, at 23.3 times the odds. Standing for most of the working day raised them 3.6 times (Riddle and colleagues, 2003).

### Why do your feet hurt from a standing desk?

Standing desk foot pain happens for the same reason any prolonged standing hurts: your feet, calves and lower legs carry a static load without the relief that walking or sitting provides. When you stand still, gravity pools blood in the lower legs, the calf muscles hold the same position without contracting and relaxing, and the plantar fascia under the arch absorbs a steady load.

A 2017 systematic review of 25 laboratory studies pooled data from 591 participants and found that clinically relevant levels of low-back symptoms developed after about 71 minutes of uninterrupted standing in the general population, but only 42 minutes in people who tend to develop pain while standing. For lower-limb symptoms, the picture was similar. The authors recommended a threshold of 40 minutes as a practical limit before breaking up standing time.

A 2015 review of the occupational health literature confirmed the association between prolonged standing and musculoskeletal discomfort, fatigue and leg pain across many types of standing work. The review also found that cardiovascular strain and leg swelling increase with standing duration.

Source: Coenen P, Parry S, Willenberg L, et al. Associations of prolonged standing with musculoskeletal symptoms: a systematic review of laboratory studies. Gait & Posture. 2017;58:310–318.
Source: Waters TR, Dick RB. Evidence of health risks associated with prolonged standing at work and intervention effectiveness. Rehabilitation Nursing. 2015;40(3):148–165.

### How long should you stand at a standing desk before sitting down?

There is no single answer that fits everyone, but the research narrows it down. A 2015 expert statement commissioned by Public Health England and the Active Working Community Interest Company recommended that desk-based workers initially build toward accumulating 2 hours per day of standing and light activity during working hours, eventually progressing to 4 hours per day. The statement specified that standing should be broken into shorter bouts, not done in one stretch.

The 2017 review of laboratory studies suggests that 40 minutes of continuous standing is the point where symptoms start to become clinically relevant. Putting those together, a practical starting point is standing for 20 to 30 minutes, sitting for 20 to 30 minutes, and repeating through the day, adjusting as your body adapts.

A 2014 systematic review of 14 studies on sit-stand workstations found sufficient evidence that they reduce low-back discomfort, with no decrease in productivity. The review found no optimal sit-stand ratio, and the authors noted that the best ratio likely varies from person to person and job to job. What the evidence supports is alternating, not a fixed rule.

Source: Buckley JP, Hedge A, Yates T, et al. The sedentary office: an expert statement on the growing case for change towards better health and productivity. British Journal of Sports Medicine. 2015;49(21):1357–1362.
Source: Coenen P, Parry S, Willenberg L, et al. Associations of prolonged standing with musculoskeletal symptoms: a systematic review of laboratory studies. Gait & Posture. 2017;58:310–318.
Source: Karakolis T, Callaghan JP. The impact of sit-stand office workstations on worker discomfort and productivity: a review. Applied Ergonomics. 2014;45(3):799–806.

### Do anti-fatigue mats help with standing desk foot pain?

Anti-fatigue mats have some evidence behind them. The 2015 occupational health review lists floor mats among the interventions with evidence for reducing discomfort during prolonged standing. A crossover study of 38 surgical team members found that standing on a 15 mm rubber anti-fatigue mat during procedures resulted in significantly lower pain and fatigue scores compared to standing on standard flooring.

The mechanism is straightforward: a softer surface lets the feet make small adjustments and shifts some of the load that a hard floor concentrates on the heel and ball of the foot. A 2018 systematic review of cushioning materials during prolonged standing noted consistent findings for reduced discomfort, though the studies were small and the benefit was for comfort, not for preventing a specific condition.

A mat is not going to solve foot pain on its own, but it is one of the simpler things to try. If you already have a standing desk and your feet hurt, a mat combined with shorter standing bouts and the exercises on this page covers the main bases.

Source: Waters TR, Dick RB. Evidence of health risks associated with prolonged standing at work and intervention effectiveness. Rehabilitation Nursing. 2015;40(3):148–165.

### What shoes should you wear at a standing desk?

If you work from home, you may be standing at your desk in socks or slippers. That is a lot of hours without any cushioning or arch support. The 2023 heel pain guideline grades orthotics on their own B-against for plantar fasciitis, meaning the evidence leans against using them as a standalone option, but that is about inserts in isolation, not about whether any shoe is better than no shoe.

A reasonable approach: wear a shoe with some cushioning and a supportive insole while you stand, even at home. You do not need a special standing-desk shoe. If you alternate between standing and sitting, you can take the shoes off during sitting periods. The exercises on this page target the tissues directly. Shoes and mats help with comfort during standing, but they do not replace the stretching and strength work.

Source: Koc TA Jr, Bise CG, Neville C, et al. Heel Pain - Plantar Fasciitis: Revision 2023. Journal of Orthopaedic & Sports Physical Therapy. 2023;53(12):CPG1–CPG39.

### What exercises can you do at your desk for standing-related foot pain?

These exercises target the calf, the plantar fascia and the small muscles of the foot. Some of them can be done at your desk during a sitting break. Others are better done away from the desk at a separate time. If any exercise brings your pain to 6 out of 10 or higher, stop for the day.

The 2023 heel pain guideline gives calf and plantar fascia stretching its top grade, A, and strength training a B. Both are for plantar fasciitis specifically, but the same tissues take the load during standing desk work. For the full plantar fasciitis exercise list, see [plantar fasciitis exercises and stretches](https://walkito.site/plantar-fasciitis-exercises/).

- **Calf stretch (straight knee)** (2 holds of 30 seconds, each leg): Step back from your desk, put your hands on the desk edge or a wall, and keep the back leg straight with the heel down. This targets the gastrocnemius, the bigger outer calf muscle. You can do this during a transition from standing to sitting.
- **Calf stretch (bent knee)** (2 holds of 30 seconds, each leg): Same position, but bend the back knee until you feel the stretch lower down, closer to the heel. The soleus, the deeper calf muscle, only lets go when the knee is bent.
- **Heel raises, seated** (3 sets of 15, both feet): Sit at your desk with feet flat on the floor. Raise both heels as high as you can, hold for a second, then lower slowly. This works the soleus, the deeper calf muscle, and you can do it during any sitting break without leaving your chair.
- **Toe spread** (3 sets of 10, hold 5 seconds): Sit at your desk and spread all five toes apart as wide as you can, then hold. This activates the small muscles between the toes that get compressed inside shoes during standing. You can do it with shoes off during a sitting break.
- **Short foot, seated** (3 sets of 10, hold 5 seconds, each foot): Sit with your foot flat on the floor. Pull the ball of the foot toward the heel so the arch lifts, without curling the toes. This trains the small muscles inside the arch that support it during standing.
- **Heel raises, both feet (standing)** (3 sets of 10, both feet): Stand at your desk, rise straight up over the big toes over about three seconds, then lower slowly. Hold the desk edge for balance. The detailed progression, including the towel variation, is in [calf raises for plantar fasciitis](https://walkito.site/calf-raises-plantar-fasciitis/).

Source: Koc TA Jr, Bise CG, Neville C, et al. Heel Pain - Plantar Fasciitis: Revision 2023. Journal of Orthopaedic & Sports Physical Therapy. 2023;53(12):CPG1–CPG39.
Source: Riddle DL, Pulisic M, Pidcoe P, Johnson RE. Risk factors for plantar fasciitis: a matched case-control study. Journal of Bone and Joint Surgery (American). 2003;85(5):872–877.

### Should you shift your weight, use a footrest, or just move more?

All three help, and all three are variations of the same idea: break up the static standing posture. The 2015 expert statement emphasises that seated work should be regularly broken up with standing, and that standing itself should include light activity. Even shifting your weight from one foot to the other changes which muscles are loaded and promotes blood flow in the lower legs.

A small footrest or a low bar under the desk lets you prop one foot up and shift the load between sides. This is an old factory-floor strategy, and it is one of the interventions the occupational health review lists. You do not need a special product for this. A sturdy box or a low shelf works.

Short movement breaks during sitting are just as important. Stand up, walk to the kitchen and back, or do a set of the seated heel raises or toe spreads from the table above. The goal is not a workout. It is avoiding the static posture that causes the problem in the first place.

Source: Buckley JP, Hedge A, Yates T, et al. The sedentary office: an expert statement on the growing case for change towards better health and productivity. British Journal of Sports Medicine. 2015;49(21):1357–1362.
Source: Waters TR, Dick RB. Evidence of health risks associated with prolonged standing at work and intervention effectiveness. Rehabilitation Nursing. 2015;40(3):148–165.

### How do you transition to a standing desk without foot pain?

Start with less standing than you think you need. The 2015 expert statement recommends building toward 2 hours of standing and light activity per day, not starting there. If you are new to standing, begin with 15 to 20 minutes of standing per hour and increase gradually over a few weeks.

A practical first week: stand for 15 minutes, sit for 45 minutes, repeat through the day. In the second week, move to 20 minutes standing, 40 sitting. By the third or fourth week, try 30 and 30. Listen to your feet and lower back. If discomfort is building, sit down sooner instead of pushing through.

Add a mat from the start if you have one. Wear shoes with some cushioning, even at home. Do the calf stretches from the table above at least once a day. If you already have foot pain from standing and want the broader guide, [why do my feet hurt after standing all day](https://walkito.site/feet-hurt-standing-all-day/) covers the overlap between standing desk pain and conditions like plantar fasciitis. For the nurse-specific version, see [foot pain for nurses](https://walkito.site/nurses-foot-pain/).

Source: Buckley JP, Hedge A, Yates T, et al. The sedentary office: an expert statement on the growing case for change towards better health and productivity. British Journal of Sports Medicine. 2015;49(21):1357–1362.

### Could standing desk foot pain be plantar fasciitis or something else?

Standing desk foot pain is usually general discomfort from prolonged static standing. But if the pain is sharp, concentrated near the heel, and worst on the first steps after you sit for a while, that pattern points toward plantar fasciitis. Standing for most of the working day raised the odds of plantar fasciitis 3.6 times in one case-control study, so the standing desk is a plausible contributor.

The exercises that help both conditions overlap heavily. If your pain follows the plantar fasciitis pattern, [plantar fasciitis exercises and stretches](https://walkito.site/plantar-fasciitis-exercises/) is the fuller guide. If your arches feel flat, see [flat feet exercises for fallen arches](https://walkito.site/flat-feet-exercises/). If you are not sure, see a clinician before loading the foot with exercise.

Source: Riddle DL, Pulisic M, Pidcoe P, Johnson RE. Risk factors for plantar fasciitis: a matched case-control study. Journal of Bone and Joint Surgery (American). 2003;85(5):872–877.

### See a clinician first if

- the pain followed an injury or a fall
- you cannot put weight on the foot, or you are limping
- the foot is numb, tingling, burning, swollen or warm
- the heel or foot is red, or you have a fever or feel unwell
- pain wakes you at night
- pain is sharp, or getting worse despite sitting more
- pain is in one pinpoint spot and gets worse with activity, which can be a stress fracture pattern and not standing discomfort
- one leg or foot has swollen suddenly and is painful, red or warm
- you have diabetes, reduced feeling in your feet or poor circulation
- the pain has not eased after several weeks of shorter standing bouts, a mat and the exercises on this page

### Doing it as a plan

You do not have to work out the order, the doses or when to progress. Walkito builds a plan one week at a time around one goal. If your standing desk pain follows the morning-pain pattern of plantar fasciitis, the first goal is morning pain at 1 out of 10 or less for 14 days in a row.

#### How long should you stand at a standing desk?

A 2015 expert statement recommends building toward 2 hours of standing and light activity per working day, eventually progressing to 4 hours, broken into shorter bouts. A 2017 systematic review found that musculoskeletal symptoms became clinically relevant after about 40 minutes of continuous standing. A practical starting point is 20 to 30 minutes of standing, followed by 20 to 30 minutes of sitting.

#### Do anti-fatigue mats actually work for standing desks?

A 2015 occupational health review lists floor mats among the interventions with evidence for reducing discomfort during prolonged standing. A crossover study of surgical team members found lower pain and fatigue scores with a 15 mm rubber mat compared to standard flooring. The benefit is for comfort and fatigue, not for preventing a specific condition. A mat combined with shorter standing bouts and calf stretches covers more than a mat alone.

#### Can a standing desk cause plantar fasciitis?

Standing for most of the working day raised the odds of plantar fasciitis 3.6 times in a case-control study of 50 cases and 100 controls. A standing desk increases your daily standing hours, so it is a plausible contributor if your calf is already tight, which was the strongest independent risk factor at 23.3 times the odds. Calf stretches are the most direct way to address both risk factors.

#### Is it better to sit or stand all day?

Neither. The 2014 Karakolis and Callaghan review found sufficient evidence that sit-stand workstations reduce low-back discomfort, with no decrease in productivity, but found no optimal sit-stand ratio. The 2017 Coenen review found that uninterrupted standing causes symptoms after about 40 minutes. Alternating between sitting and standing is what the evidence supports, not choosing one or the other.

#### What exercises can you do at a standing desk?

During standing: calf stretches against the desk edge (2 holds of 30 seconds each side) and standing heel raises (3 sets of 10). During sitting breaks: seated heel raises (3 sets of 15), toe spreads and the short foot exercise. These target the calf, plantar fascia and intrinsic foot muscles that carry the standing load. If any exercise takes your pain to 6 out of 10 or higher, stop for the day.

#### Why do my feet hurt more standing still than walking?

Walking activates the calf pump, which pushes blood back up from the lower legs with each step. Standing still takes that pump away, so blood pools in the feet and lower legs, and the muscles hold the same static position instead of contracting and relaxing. A 2017 systematic review confirmed this mechanism and found lower-limb symptoms develop reliably during static standing in laboratory settings.

## Best app for plantar fasciitis: a buyer's guide for 2026

Language: English · https://walkito.site/best-app-for-plantar-fasciitis/ · published 2026-10-04 · updated 2026-10-04

This page compares seven apps that include exercises for plantar fasciitis, flat feet or general foot pain. Walkito is one of them, and Walkito makes this page, so you should know that up front. The goal is to be fair, say where others are stronger, and give you enough detail to pick the one that fits your situation.

- The 2023 clinical guideline for heel pain gives plantar fascia and calf stretching a grade of A and strength training a grade of B. A good app should include both.
- Pain adaptation matters: a fixed daily routine cannot tell a good morning from a bad one, and loading an inflamed fascia the same way every day can set you back.
- Exakt Health is the strongest option for runners recovering from plantar fasciitis who also want a return-to-running plan, and it is certified as a medical device in the EU.
- Hinge Health is free through employers and health plans and comes with a full clinical care team, but you cannot buy it yourself.
- No app can diagnose your foot pain. If your pain followed an injury, comes with swelling or numbness, or wakes you at night, see a clinician before starting any program.

### What should a plantar fasciitis app actually do?

A useful plantar fasciitis app should include exercises that match what the research supports. The 2023 clinical guideline for heel pain grades the evidence behind each approach. Plantar fascia and calf stretching earn an A, the top grade. Strength training earns a B. That means both should be in the app, not just one.

Beyond the exercise list, these are the things worth checking before you subscribe:

- **Progression.** Exercises should get harder over time, not stay at the same level forever. The research behind strength training for plantar fasciitis used a progressive loading protocol.
- **Pain adaptation.** The app should respond when pain is worse. Loading a painful heel the same way on a bad morning is the fastest way to lose someone's trust in the program.
- **Time per day.** Most people will not do 30 minutes of foot exercises. Five to ten minutes of the right exercises, done consistently, is more realistic.
- **Price and trial.** Know what you are paying and whether there is a free trial to see if it works for you.
- **Platforms.** Some apps are iOS only. If you use Android, your choices are narrower.
- **Privacy.** Pain and health data is sensitive. Check whether the app shares or sells it.
- **Clinician involvement.** An app built or reviewed by licensed physiotherapists or physical therapists is a reasonable signal. An app that can connect you to a clinician is a stronger one.

Source: Koc TA Jr, Bise CG, Neville C, et al. Heel Pain - Plantar Fasciitis: Revision 2023. Journal of Orthopaedic & Sports Physical Therapy. 2023;53(12):CPG1–CPG39.

### How do these apps compare?

The table below covers seven apps available in October 2026. Every fact was checked against the app's own App Store or Google Play listing and its official website. Ratings and review counts are as shown on the iOS App Store at the time of writing.

### Exakt Health: the runner's rehab app

Exakt Health is built for runners, and it shows. The app has over 15 injury rehab plans, from plantar fasciitis to Achilles tendinopathy to meniscus tears, plus running training plans from couch to marathon. Each rehab plan ends with a structured return-to-running phase, which is something most foot pain apps do not offer.

It is certified as a medical device in the EU, which means it has passed regulatory review for safety and intended use. It was built by licensed sports physiotherapists and running coaches. The app has 600+ exercise videos and adapts its plan as you progress through levels.

At $19.99 a month or $59.99 for six months, Exakt is not cheap, but the breadth of conditions and the quality of its rehab plans are hard to match in the self-serve app market. The 7-day free trial lets you see the full app before paying. It is available in English, French, German and Spanish, on both iOS and Android.

Where Exakt is stronger than Walkito: more injury types covered (15+ versus heel pain, flat feet and shins), a full return-to-running program, Android availability, EU medical device certification, and an established user base with a 4.8 rating across 125 iOS reviews.

Where Walkito differs: Walkito adjusts each day's session from a morning pain check-in rather than end-of-session feedback, tests left-right asymmetry every 14 days, and focuses specifically on heel and foot pain rather than the full range of running injuries.

### Hinge Health: the employer-sponsored option

Hinge Health is the largest digital MSK platform in the United States, with over 2 million members. If your employer or health plan covers it, it is free to you and comes with something no self-serve app can match: a dedicated care team that includes physical therapists, orthopedic doctors and other specialists.

The app covers a wide range of joint and muscle conditions, not just feet. It also includes the Enso wearable device for acute pain relief. The 4.9 rating across 168,000 iOS reviews reflects the combination of guided exercises, human coaching and zero cost.

The catch is access. You cannot buy Hinge Health from the App Store. You need coverage through one of the 2,800+ employers or health plans that offer it. If you have access, it is likely the most complete option on this list. If you do not, it is not an option at all.

Hinge Health is not foot-specific. It covers back, knee, hip and neck pain as its primary use cases. For plantar fasciitis specifically, a more focused app may be a better starting point.

### Prehab: the broadest exercise library

The Prehab Guys app is built by Doctors of Physical Therapy and has the widest exercise library in this comparison: 55+ programs, 170+ workouts and 4,000+ exercise videos. It has a specific plantar fasciitis rehab program. The Body Scan feature asks about your pain, goals and movement needs, then recommends a program.

At $49 a month or about $200 a year, it is the most expensive self-serve option here. The 7-day free trial is on the annual plan only. Sessions run about 20 minutes, which is longer than the 3-to-10-minute range of foot-focused apps. The quality of the video instruction is consistently praised in reviews.

Prehab is a good fit if you have pain in multiple areas and want a single app that covers everything from shoulders to feet. It is less focused than apps built specifically for plantar fasciitis, and it does not adapt daily sessions based on your morning pain.

It is iOS only and English only.

### PlantarCare: the free tracker

PlantarCare is free, has no in-app purchases, and does not require an account. It focuses entirely on heel pain and plantar fasciitis. You log your morning first-step pain and worst daytime pain, and the app moves you through recovery stages with guided stretches, calf work, heel raises and icing reminders matched to your stage.

For a free app, it does a surprising amount right: pain trending over time, footwear and load logging, and red-flag reminders that tell you when to see a clinician. The trade-off is that it is new, has no ratings yet, and does not describe the research behind its exercise selection.

PlantarCare is a reasonable starting point if you want to track your pain for free and follow basic stretches without committing to a subscription. It is iOS only.

### Arch: Flat Feet Trainer

Arch is the only app in this comparison focused entirely on flat feet and arch strengthening. It has 40+ foot exercises, progress tracking and a clean design. At $39.99 a year or $9.99 a month, with a 7-day free trial, the price is moderate.

A reviewer noted that the app lacks exercise videos, using illustrations instead. The app claims its routines are "backed by science" and "proven physiotherapy principles" but does not cite specific studies. With only 6 ratings on the App Store, it is early in its life.

If your primary concern is flat feet without significant pain, Arch is worth trying. For plantar fasciitis, it is not the right fit since it does not include heel-specific rehab exercises or pain tracking.

### Plantar Fasciitis Exercises: a basic app with a paywall

This app by Verdhit Agarwal offers 15 exercises across three levels: gentle stretches, strength building and advanced drills. It is listed as free on both iOS and Android, but both store listings show in-app purchases, and one reviewer reported being asked to pay for a monthly membership before they could use it.

The exercises are basic, with text instructions rather than video demonstration. There is no progression logic, no pain tracking and no adaptation. The single iOS rating is 1 out of 5, and that review is specifically about being charged unexpectedly. It is the kind of app that exists because "plantar fasciitis exercises" is a high-volume search term, not because someone built a thoughtful program.

If you want a free reference for what stretches to try, check the store listing before you start since some exercises may sit behind a paywall. For an actual guided program with progression, it is not enough.

### Walkito: what it does and what it does not

Walkito is an exercise program for heel pain, flat feet and lower-leg pain. It was released on the App Store on October 2, 2026. It is new, has no ratings yet, and is iOS only.

What it does: builds a weekly plan from your answers about pain, goals and schedule. Each morning, a check-in adjusts that day's session to how your foot feels. Tests every 14 days measure calf raises, arch hold and single-leg balance, and compare left to right. Sessions are 3, 5 or 10 minutes. Exercises follow the 2023 heel pain guideline and the Rathleff 2015 trial. It connects to Apple Health for steps, sleep and walking data, which stay on your phone.

What it does not: it does not diagnose your pain, it is not a medical device, it has no clinician on the other end and it is not available on Android. It covers heel pain, flat feet and shin pain, not the 15+ injury types Exakt covers or the full-body scope of Hinge Health or Prehab.

At $44.99 a year or $7.99 a week, the annual price is lower than most competitors. The weekly price is higher relative to the annual, which is standard subscription pricing.

Source: Koc TA Jr, Bise CG, Neville C, et al. Heel Pain - Plantar Fasciitis: Revision 2023. Journal of Orthopaedic & Sports Physical Therapy. 2023;53(12):CPG1–CPG39.
Source: Rathleff MS, Mølgaard CM, Fredberg U, et al. High-load strength training improves outcome in patients with plantar fasciitis: a randomized controlled trial with 12-month follow-up. Scandinavian Journal of Medicine & Science in Sports. 2015;25(3):e292–e300.

### How to choose

Start from your situation, not from feature lists.

- **You are a runner with plantar fasciitis** and want a structured return to running: [Exakt Health](https://www.exakthealth.com/) is the strongest fit.
- **Your employer covers Hinge Health**: check your eligibility. A care team with PTs and doctors is hard to beat at zero cost.
- **You have pain in several body areas**, not just your feet: [Prehab](https://theprehabguys.com/) gives you 55+ programs in one subscription.
- **You want a free starting point** to track heel pain and try basic stretches: [PlantarCare](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/plantarcare-heel-pain-tracker/id6789899136) does that well for no cost.
- **Your main issue is flat feet** without significant pain: [Arch: Flat Feet Trainer](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/arch-flat-feet-trainer/id6755728858) is focused on exactly that.
- **You want a daily plan for heel pain or flat feet that adjusts to your morning** and tests your progress: that is what [Walkito](https://walkito.site/) was built for.

### When an app is not enough, see a clinician

- your pain followed an injury or a fall
- you cannot put weight on the foot or you are limping
- the pain comes with numbness, tingling, burning, swelling or warmth
- the heel is red, or you have a fever
- pain wakes you at night or is present at rest
- both feet hurt and other joints are swollen or stiff
- pain is getting worse week over week despite exercise
- you have diabetes, reduced feeling in your feet or poor circulation

### Doing it as a plan

If you have read this far and Walkito sounds like a fit, here is how it works. You answer a few questions about where it hurts, which side, how active you are and your goal. Walkito builds a weekly plan around those answers. Each morning, a check-in adjusts the day. Every 14 days, a short test measures calf endurance, arch hold and single-leg balance.

#### Is there a free app for plantar fasciitis?

PlantarCare is free with no in-app purchases. It tracks morning pain, suggests stretches matched to your recovery stage, and shows trends over time. The "Plantar Fasciitis Exercises" app is listed as free but shows in-app purchases on the store, and a reviewer reported being charged to use it. PlantarCare is the more reliably free option of the two.

#### What exercises should a plantar fasciitis app include?

The 2023 clinical guideline for heel pain gives plantar fascia and calf stretching a grade of A and strength training a grade of B. A good app should include both: stretching for the fascia and calf, and progressive calf strengthening such as heel raises. Exercises that progress in difficulty and adapt to your pain level are more useful than a static list.

#### Is Exakt Health better than Walkito for plantar fasciitis?

Exakt Health covers more conditions, including 15+ running injuries and full run training plans. It is on both iOS and Android and is certified as a medical device in the EU. Walkito focuses specifically on heel and foot pain with daily pain-based adaptation and 14-day progress tests. Exakt is the stronger choice for runners who need rehab plus a running plan. Walkito is narrower but adjusts each session to your morning.

#### Can an app replace seeing a physical therapist for plantar fasciitis?

No app replaces a clinician who can examine your foot, rule out other causes and adjust a plan in real time. An app is useful for guided daily exercises between visits, or as a starting point when pain is mild and matches the typical plantar fasciitis pattern. If pain came from an injury, comes with swelling or numbness, or is getting worse, see a clinician first.

#### Is Hinge Health free?

Hinge Health is free to members whose employer or health plan covers it. You cannot buy it directly from the App Store. Check eligibility at hinge.health/covered. If you are covered, it includes a care team with physical therapists and doctors at no cost to you.

#### Why does Walkito not call itself the best app for plantar fasciitis?

Because it would not be honest. Walkito is new, has no user ratings yet, covers fewer conditions than Exakt Health, and has no clinician on the other end like Hinge Health. What it does well is adjust each day to your pain and test your progress every 14 days. Whether that makes it the right app for you depends on what you need.

#### Do any of these apps work on Android?

Exakt Health and Hinge Health are on both iOS and Android. "Plantar Fasciitis Exercises" is also on both, though it shows in-app purchases on each store. Walkito, Prehab, PlantarCare and Arch are currently iOS only. If you use Android, Exakt Health is the most feature-complete option for foot pain.

## Walkito vs Exakt Health: which one fits you?

Language: English · https://walkito.site/walkito-vs-exakt-health/ · published 2026-10-04 · updated 2026-10-04

Walkito and Exakt Health both offer exercise-based plans for plantar fasciitis, but they are built for different people. Exakt is a runner's app with 15+ injury rehab plans and a return-to-running program. Walkito is a narrower app focused on heel pain, flat feet and daily pain adaptation. This page compares them honestly, says where Exakt is the better choice, and explains what Walkito does differently.

- Exakt Health covers 15+ running injuries and includes running training plans from 5K to marathon. Walkito covers heel pain, flat feet and shin pain only.
- Exakt is on both iOS and Android. Walkito is iOS only as of October 2026.
- Exakt Health is certified as a medical device in the EU. Walkito is not a medical device.
- Walkito adjusts each session from a morning pain check-in and tests left-right asymmetry every 14 days. Exakt adapts its plan from end-of-session feedback.
- Exakt costs $19.99/month or $59.99 for six months. Walkito costs $44.99/year or $7.99/week.

### Side-by-side comparison

Every Exakt fact below was checked against the Exakt Health App Store listing, Google Play listing and exakthealth.com in October 2026. Every Walkito fact comes from the Walkito App Store listing, walkito.site and the app's own source code.

### Who is Exakt Health built for?

Exakt Health is built for runners. That is its core identity, and everything in the app reflects it. If you are a runner recovering from plantar fasciitis, Achilles tendinopathy, an ankle sprain, a hamstring strain or a meniscus tear, Exakt has a specific rehab plan for your injury. It covers over 15 different conditions.

Each rehab plan ends with a walk-run return-to-running program, which is one of the hardest parts of recovery to get right on your own. The app also has running training plans for every distance from couch to 5K through to marathon.

Exakt was founded in 2021 by Philip Billaudelle, Lucia Payo and Maryke Louw. It is built by licensed sports physiotherapists and running coaches, and it raised about EUR 2.2 million in seed funding in September 2024. The team is based in Berlin. The app is certified as a medical device in the EU, meaning it has passed regulatory review for its intended use.

If you are a runner who needs both injury rehab and a structured training plan, Exakt is hard to match. Its 4.8 rating across 125 iOS reviews and 100K+ Android downloads show that it works for its audience.

### Who is Walkito built for?

Walkito is built for people whose feet hurt and who want a short daily exercise plan that adjusts to how they feel each morning. That includes plantar fasciitis, flexible flat feet, and shin pain. It is also built for people on their feet all day: nurses, retail workers, warehouse staff.

The app is narrower than Exakt. It does not cover knee injuries, hamstring strains or running plans. What it does differently is adjust each day's session from a morning pain check-in rather than end-of-session feedback. A morning of 7/10 or higher switches the day to about three minutes of seated work. A big day on your feet (measured through Apple Health steps) turns the next strength session into a lighter recovery one.

Walkito tests progress every 14 days with calf raises, an arch hold and single-leg balance, and compares your left side with your right. That left-right comparison is something most apps in this space do not track.

Walkito was released on October 2, 2026. It is new, has no user ratings yet, and is iOS only. It does not have the track record or breadth that Exakt has built since 2021.

### How does each app build your plan?

Exakt asks about your injury, your experience level, and your weekly schedule, then assigns you a structured rehab plan with levels. You progress through levels based on how each session goes. When rehab is done, you can switch directly to a running training plan without starting over.

Walkito asks about pain location, which side, your activity level, your goal, and how many days and minutes you have. It builds a weekly plan around measured goals: pain-free mornings, a 60-second arch hold, 25 single-leg calf raises, 30-second single-leg balance, and left-right symmetry. Each week it rebuilds the plan from how the previous week went. One goal is the focus at a time. When a goal is reached, it moves to maintaining and the next goal starts.

The main difference: Exakt follows a structured level-based progression. Walkito follows a goal-based progression where each morning's check-in adjusts the day's intensity.

### Conditions covered

This is where Exakt is clearly stronger. Its rehab plans cover plantar fasciitis, Achilles tendinopathy, ankle sprains, hamstring strains, meniscus tears, runner's knee and more. If your pain is in your knee, hip or hamstring, Walkito does not have a plan for it.

Walkito covers plantar fasciitis, flat feet (flexible), heel pain from standing, and shin pain. Its exercises follow the 2023 heel pain guideline (stretching grade A, strength grade B) and the Rathleff 2015 trial (loaded heel raises for plantar fasciitis). For those specific conditions, it has exercises, progression logic and pain adaptation. For anything outside that scope, Exakt or a broader app like Prehab is the right choice.

Source: Koc TA Jr, Bise CG, Neville C, et al. Heel Pain - Plantar Fasciitis: Revision 2023. Journal of Orthopaedic & Sports Physical Therapy. 2023;53(12):CPG1–CPG39.
Source: Rathleff MS, Mølgaard CM, Fredberg U, et al. High-load strength training improves outcome in patients with plantar fasciitis: a randomized controlled trial with 12-month follow-up. Scandinavian Journal of Medicine & Science in Sports. 2015;25(3):e292–e300.

### Price comparison

Walkito costs $44.99 per year or $7.99 per week. The annual price works out to about $0.87 per week. No free trial is listed on the App Store, though the terms of use allow for introductory offers.

Exakt costs $19.99 per month for rehab plans, with 3-month ($39.99) and 6-month ($59.99) options. Running training plans go up to $99.99 per year. Every subscription starts with a 7-day free trial.

Over a full year: Walkito annual is $44.99. Exakt's cheapest rehab option (6-month plan renewed twice) is about $120. If you include a running plan, Exakt can exceed $200 per year.

If you need only heel or foot pain exercises, Walkito is significantly cheaper. If you need running injury rehab plus a training plan, Exakt's higher price covers more.

### Platforms and languages

Exakt Health is on both iOS and Android. If you use an Android phone, this is the deciding factor by itself since Walkito is iOS only.

Exakt supports English, French, German and Spanish. Walkito supports English, Russian and Spanish. The overlap is English and Spanish. If you need French or German, Exakt is the only option. If you need Russian, Walkito is the only option.

### Privacy

Walkito reads Apple Health data (steps, sleep, walking asymmetry, walking speed, resting heart rate) and keeps it on the device. It is never uploaded. What gets synced to the Walkito account is pain scores, session data and test results. There is no ad tracking.

Exakt Health's App Store privacy label lists Identifiers as data used to track you, and Purchases, Identifiers, Usage Data and Diagnostics as data collected but not linked to your identity. Its Google Play listing states no data is shared with third parties, financial data may be collected, data is encrypted in transit and deletion is available.

Both apps collect standard usage data. Neither sells health data. Walkito's on-device approach to Apple Health data is a stricter privacy model.

### Evidence base

Exakt Health is certified as a medical device in the EU (Germany), which requires evidence of safety and intended purpose. The app is built by licensed sports physiotherapists. It states that its methods are evidence-based but does not list specific studies on its App Store listing or pricing page.

Walkito lists its evidence sources on its website. Its exercises follow the 2023 clinical guideline for heel pain (Koc et al., JOSPT), the Rathleff 2015 trial on heavy heel raises, the Brijwasi 2023 trial on flat feet exercises, and others. Each exercise in the app carries an evidence level (Strong, Moderate, or Early) with a one-line explanation.

Neither app has published its own clinical trial. Both rely on existing research applied through their respective programs.

Source: Koc TA Jr, Bise CG, Neville C, et al. Heel Pain - Plantar Fasciitis: Revision 2023. Journal of Orthopaedic & Sports Physical Therapy. 2023;53(12):CPG1–CPG39.
Source: Rathleff MS, Mølgaard CM, Fredberg U, et al. High-load strength training improves outcome in patients with plantar fasciitis: a randomized controlled trial with 12-month follow-up. Scandinavian Journal of Medicine & Science in Sports. 2015;25(3):e292–e300.

### When to pick Exakt Health over Walkito

Pick Exakt Health if any of the following is true:

- You are a runner recovering from a running injury and want a structured return-to-running plan.
- Your injury is not plantar fasciitis or flat feet. Exakt covers 15+ conditions; Walkito covers three.
- You use an Android phone.
- You want a 7-day free trial to test the app before paying.
- EU medical device certification matters to you.
- You need the app in French or German.

### When to pick Walkito over Exakt Health

Pick Walkito if any of the following is true:

- Your pain is specifically heel pain, plantar fasciitis or flat feet, and you want a focused program for that.
- You want sessions of 3 to 10 minutes rather than 15 to 30.
- Daily pain adaptation from a morning check-in matters more to you than level-based progression.
- You want progress tests every 14 days that compare left to right.
- Price is a factor: Walkito at $44.99 per year is less than half of Exakt's lowest annual cost.
- You need the app in Russian.
- You are on your feet all day for work, not running, and want an app built for that.

### When an app is not enough, see a clinician

- your pain followed an injury or a fall
- you cannot put weight on the foot or you are limping
- the pain comes with numbness, tingling, burning, swelling or warmth
- pain wakes you at night or is present at rest
- squeezing the sides of the heel hurts, which can point to a stress fracture rather than plantar fasciitis
- pain is getting worse week over week despite consistent exercise
- you have diabetes, reduced feeling in your feet or poor circulation

### Doing it as a plan

If Walkito sounds like the right fit for your situation, here is how it works. You answer questions about where it hurts, which side, your activity level and your goal. Walkito builds a weekly plan around measured goals, starting with pain-free mornings. Each morning, one check-in adjusts the day.

#### Is Exakt Health better than Walkito?

It depends on what you need. Exakt Health covers 15+ running injuries and includes return-to-running plans. It is on both iOS and Android and is certified as a medical device in the EU. Walkito is focused on heel pain and flat feet, with daily pain adaptation and shorter sessions. For runners with multiple injury types, Exakt is the stronger fit. For heel-specific pain with daily adjustment, Walkito was built for that.

#### Is Walkito cheaper than Exakt Health?

Yes, on an annual basis. Walkito costs $44.99 per year. Exakt Health's cheapest rehab option is $59.99 for six months, or about $120 per year. Exakt offers a 7-day free trial; Walkito does not currently list one on the App Store.

#### Does Exakt Health have a plantar fasciitis plan?

Yes. Exakt Health has a specific plantar fasciitis rehab plan, along with plans for Achilles tendinopathy, ankle sprains, hamstring strains, meniscus tears and more. The plantar fasciitis plan ends with a walk-run program to return to running safely, and the app adapts the plan as you progress through its levels.

#### Can I use Walkito on Android?

Not yet. Walkito is iOS only as of October 2026. Android is planned but no release date has been announced. If you use Android, Exakt Health is available on Google Play with a plantar fasciitis rehab plan, and it works on both Android and iOS today.

#### Is Exakt Health a medical device?

Yes. Exakt Health is certified as a medical device in the EU (Germany). This means it has passed regulatory review for safety and its intended use. Walkito is not a medical device and does not claim to diagnose or provide medical advice.

#### Which app adapts more to daily pain?

Walkito adjusts each session from a morning pain check-in before you start. A score of 7/10 or higher makes the session lighter. A big step-count day triggers a recovery session the next day. Exakt adapts its plan from how you rate each session after you finish it. Walkito's approach is more reactive to daily pain changes; Exakt's is more focused on overall plan progression.

## Упражнения и растяжка при плантарном фасциите и боли в пятке

Language: Russian (Русский) · https://walkito.site/ru/bol-v-pyatke-uprazhneniya/ · published 2026-09-24 · updated 2026-09-28

Первые шаги с кровати самая тяжёлая часть дня. Резко тянет прямо в пятке, ещё до утреннего кофе. Когда вы расходитесь, становится легче, а после того как посидите, боль возвращается. У этой картины есть название, плантарный фасциит, и клинические рекомендации 2023 года называют его самой частой известной причиной боли в пятке под стопой.

- Клинические рекомендации 2023 года по боли в пятке из Journal of Orthopaedic & Sports Physical Therapy дают растяжке подошвенной фасции и икр высший уровень, A, а силовым упражнениям уровень B.
- В исследовании с участием 48 человек тяжёлые подъёмы на носки быстрее растяжки уменьшили боль и улучшили повседневную функцию, а через двенадцать месяцев результаты групп сравнялись (Rathleff и соавторы, 2015).
- Если пятка болит при беге, те же рекомендации советуют менять нагрузку, а не бросать всё. У этого совета уровень E: он основан на теории, а не на исследованиях.
- Сначала обратитесь к врачу, если боль появилась после травмы, сопровождается онемением или отёком, будит вас ночью или пятка болит при сжатии.

### Упражнения при плантарном фасциите и стартовые дозировки

При плантарном фасциите в Walkito есть растяжка подошвенной фасции и икр, силовая работа для икр, которая наращивается маленькими шагами, и прокатывание стопы. Это стартовые дозировки Walkito, а не назначение. [Как написаны эти гайды](https://walkito.site/ru/o-proekte/).

Порядок важен. Пока цель связана с болью, Walkito держит работу для икр мягкой: сначала подъёмы на носки сидя, потом подъёмы на носки на двух ногах, потом удержание на носках, по одной ступени за раз. На следующую ступень вы переходите, когда два последних занятия с ней дались легко. Подъёмы на носки с полотенцем нагружают подошвенную фасцию сильнее всего, поэтому они появляются только тогда, когда утренняя боль снизилась и цель сменилась на силу икр. Если какое-то упражнение поднимает боль до **6 из 10 или выше**, на сегодня остановитесь. На этой отметке Walkito завершает занятие.

- **Растяжка подошвенной фасции** (2 удержания по 30 секунд, каждая стопа): Сядьте и положите стопу на колено другой ноги. Потяните пальцы на себя, пока не почувствуете растяжение в своде, а не в икре. Первую растяжку сделайте на краю кровати, ещё до того, как стопа коснётся пола.
- **Растяжка икры** (2 удержания по 30 секунд, каждая нога): Упритесь руками в стену. Задняя нога прямая, пятка на полу, таз подан вперёд. Напряжённая икра весь день тянет пятку, поэтому эта растяжка важна, хотя чувствуется выше.
- **Растяжка камбаловидной мышцы** (2 удержания по 30 секунд, каждая нога): Встаньте так же, затем согните колено задней ноги, пока растяжение не уйдёт ниже, к пятке. Камбаловидная мышца, более глубокая мышца икры, расслабляется только при согнутом колене.
- **Подъёмы на носки сидя** (3 подхода по 10, обе стопы): Сядьте, стопы на полу, и поднимайтесь на подушечки стоп. Руки на коленях добавят сопротивления. Подъёмы на носки сидя тренируют икры почти без нагрузки на пятку.
- **Подъёмы на носки на двух ногах** (3 подхода по 10, обе стопы): Встаньте на обе стопы, поднимитесь прямо вверх над большими пальцами и медленно опуститесь. Обе стопы делят нагрузку, пока икры просыпаются.
- **Удержание на носках** (3 удержания по 20 секунд, обе стопы): Поднимитесь на носки обеих стоп и замрите наверху. Не проседайте. Удержание наверху нагружает сухожилие без пружинящих движений.
- **Подъёмы на носки с полотенцем** (4 подхода по 10, каждая нога, с дополнительным весом): Встаньте одной ногой на ступеньку, под пальцами свёрнутое полотенце. Поднимайтесь три секунды, задержитесь наверху на две и опускайтесь три секунды. На этом уровне Walkito добавляет вес, например рюкзак. Именно полотенце заставляет это упражнение работать на подошвенную фасцию, а не только на икру.
- **Прокатывание стопы** (1 минута): Сядьте и медленно прокатывайте подошву по массажному мячу с плотным давлением. Если морщитесь от боли, ослабьте давление. Прокатывание успокаивает ткани после работы. Нет мяча? Массаж стопы делается плотными движениями большого пальца руки от пятки к пальцам.

### Что помогает при утренней боли в пятке?

Утренняя боль в пятке на первых шагах чаще всего связана с плантарным фасциитом. Она обычно проходит, когда вы расходитесь, и возвращается, после того как вы посидите.

На неё нацелены две вещи на этой странице. Растяжку подошвенной фасции делают **ещё до того, как встать**, на краю кровати, потянув пальцы на себя, чтобы первые шаги не были первой растяжкой. А клинические рекомендации 2023 года дают ночным ортезам, которые носят от 1 до 3 месяцев, уровень **A** для тех, у кого утром на первых шагах боль возвращается снова и снова. Ночной ортез стоит обсудить с врачом. Walkito их не предоставляет.

По той же причине Walkito каждый день спрашивает об утренней боли. Утренняя боль яснее всего показывает, как стопа справилась со вчерашним днём, и от неё зависит, сколько сегодняшнее занятие от вас потребует.

Source: Koc TA Jr, Bise CG, Neville C, et al. Heel Pain - Plantar Fasciitis: Revision 2023. Journal of Orthopaedic & Sports Physical Therapy. 2023;53(12):CPG1–CPG39.

### Отдыхать или продолжать бегать, если болит пятка?

Если пятка при плантарном фасциите болит при беге, меняйте нагрузку, а не бросайте всё. Клинические рекомендации 2023 года советуют научиться регулировать нагрузку на стопы на работе, в спорте и в повседневной жизни. У этого совета уровень E: он основан на теории, а не на исследованиях. Поэтому растягивайтесь каждый день и сокращайте то, от чего пятке хуже.

В плохое утро оставьте растяжку и уберите подъёмы на носки на этот день. Следующее утро покажет, как всё прошло. Если после пробежки первые шаги заметно хуже, эта пробежка была для пятки слишком большой нагрузкой. Walkito читает это так же. Насыщенный день на ногах превращает следующее силовое занятие в лёгкое восстановительное, а болезненное утро делает занятие короче, но не отменяет его.

Остановитесь и обратитесь к врачу, если бегать остро больно или боль усиливается неделю за неделей. То же самое, если боль нарастает во время пробежек после того, как вы увеличили объём бега, или если больно сжимать пятку с боков. И то и другое может быть признаком стрессового перелома, одной из других причин боли в пятке, которые называют рекомендации.

Source: Koc TA Jr, Bise CG, Neville C, et al. Heel Pain - Plantar Fasciitis: Revision 2023. Journal of Orthopaedic & Sports Physical Therapy. 2023;53(12):CPG1–CPG39.

### Что лучше при плантарном фасциите: силовые упражнения или растяжка?

При плантарном фасциите помогают и силовые упражнения, и растяжка, а силовые помогают раньше.

В исследовании с участием 48 человек с плантарным фасциитом, подтверждённым на УЗИ, все носили стельки. Одна группа добавила тяжёлые подъёмы на носки через день. Другая каждый день растягивала подошвенную фасцию. Через три месяца группа с подъёмами на носки заметно опережала по боли и повседневной функции. Через двенадцать месяцев группы сравнялись. Силовая работа ускорила улучшение, но не сделала его больше.

Рекомендации поддерживают и то и другое. Разбор по каждому исследованию есть на [странице с исследованиями](https://walkito.site/science/) (на английском).

Source: Rathleff MS, Mølgaard CM, Fredberg U, et al. High-load strength training improves outcome in patients with plantar fasciitis: a randomized controlled trial with 12-month follow-up. Scandinavian Journal of Medicine & Science in Sports. 2015;25(3):e292–e300.

### Что советуют клинические рекомендации 2023 года при плантарном фасциите?

Клинические рекомендации 2023 года по плантарному фасцииту оценивают каждый вариант по силе доказательств. Высший уровень обозначается буквой A. Уровень с пометкой «против» значит, что рекомендации советуют этот вариант не использовать.

Source: Koc TA Jr, Bise CG, Neville C, et al. Heel Pain - Plantar Fasciitis: Revision 2023. Journal of Orthopaedic & Sports Physical Therapy. 2023;53(12):CPG1–CPG39.

### Что происходит, когда пятка перестаёт болеть?

Когда боль в пятке проходит, Walkito продолжает с меньшей дозировкой, потому что боль в пятке может вернуться. Когда вы достигаете цели «Лёгкие утра» (утренняя боль не выше 1 из 10 14 дней подряд), цель переходит в поддержание, а её место занимает следующая.

Если у вас ещё и плоские своды, для свода есть свои упражнения и свои сроки: смотрите [упражнения при плоскостопии](https://walkito.site/ru/ploskostopie-uprazhneniya/). Ответы на вопросы о самом приложении есть в [FAQ](https://walkito.site/faq/) (на английском).

### Сначала обратитесь к врачу, если

- боль появилась после травмы или падения
- на ногу нельзя наступить или вы хромаете
- боль сопровождается онемением, покалыванием, жжением, отёком или ощущением жара
- пятка покраснела, у вас температура или общее недомогание
- боль будит вас ночью
- боль острая или усиливается, хотя вы снизили нагрузку
- больно сжимать пятку с боков или боль нарастает во время пробежек после того, как вы увеличили объём бега: и то и другое может быть признаком стрессового перелома
- у вас диабет, сниженная чувствительность стоп или плохое кровообращение
- болят обе пятки, а другие суставы опухают или скованы
- за несколько недель упражнений и сниженной нагрузки лучше не стало
- свод одной стопы резко опустился уже во взрослом возрасте

### Всё это как план

Вам не нужно самим разбираться с порядком, дозировками и тем, сколько оставаться на каждом упражнении. Walkito строит план по одной неделе вокруг одной цели. При боли в пятке первая цель называется «Лёгкие утра»: боль не выше 1 из 10 14 дней подряд.

#### Можно ли бегать при плантарном фасциите?

Бросать всё не обязательно. Лучше измените нагрузку. Клинические рекомендации 2023 года советуют научиться регулировать нагрузку на стопы, с уровнем E: совет основан на теории, а не на исследованиях. Сократите то, от чего пятке хуже, и растягивайтесь каждый день. Если на следующее утро первые шаги заметно хуже, пробежка была слишком большой нагрузкой. При острой или усиливающейся боли нужен врач.

#### Почему пятка болит сильнее по утрам?

Боль в пятке на первых шагах после сна или сидения чаще всего связана с плантарным фасциитом. Обычное объяснение такое: ткани под стопой в покое становятся жёстче, а первые шаги резко их нагружают. Поэтому растяжку подошвенной фасции делают ещё до того, как встать, и поэтому клинические рекомендации 2023 года дают ночным ортезам при такой боли уровень A.

#### Что лучше при плантарном фасциите: растяжка или укрепление?

Помогает и то и другое, а укрепление действует быстрее. В исследовании с участием 48 человек тяжёлые подъёмы на носки через три месяца заметно опережали растяжку, но через двенадцать месяцев группы сравнялись. Клинические рекомендации 2023 года дают растяжке уровень A, а силовым упражнениям уровень B. Подробности на [странице с исследованиями](https://walkito.site/science/) (на английском).

#### Пяточная шпора и плантарный фасциит: это одно и то же?

Не совсем. «Пяточной шпорой» часто называют плантарный фасциит, но, строго говоря, шпорой называют костный вырост, который виден на рентгене. А плантарный фасциит означает боль в полосе ткани под стопой. На этой странице собраны упражнения, которые клинические рекомендации 2023 года оценивают при боли в пятке под стопой. Что именно стоит за вашей болью, может сказать только врач.

#### Как часто делать упражнения при плантарном фасциите?

Растягивайтесь в большинство дней, а силовую работу для икр делайте в силовые дни. В Walkito вы выбираете 3, 5 или 7 тренировочных дней в неделю, и в каждой неделе три силовых дня, никогда два подряд. Растяжка входит в большинство занятий, а первую растяжку подошвенной фасции вы делаете, ещё не поставив стопу на пол. В исследовании, на которое опирается Walkito, подъёмы на носки делали через день.

#### Когда идти к врачу с болью в пятке?

Сначала обратитесь к врачу, если боль появилась после травмы или падения, на ногу нельзя наступить или боль сопровождается онемением, покалыванием, отёком, ощущением жара или температурой. То же самое, если она будит вас ночью, острая или усиливается или если больно сжимать пятку: это может быть стрессовый перелом. Walkito не ставит диагнозов.

## Упражнения при плоскостопии и боли в своде стопы

Language: Russian (Русский) · https://walkito.site/ru/ploskostopie-uprazhneniya/ · published 2026-09-24 · updated 2026-09-28

К вечеру стопы устают, а своды ноют. Когда вы стоите, стопы будто заваливаются внутрь, а своды опускаются к полу. Вам могут сказать, что плоскостопие у вас от природы и думать о нём не стоит. Желание что-то с ним сделать вполне понятно, и тренировке свода посвящены настоящие исследования.

- Рандомизированное исследование на этой странице проводилось при гибком плоскостопии, когда свод возвращается, если стопа не касается пола (Brijwasi и Borkar, 2023).
- В этом исследовании с участием 52 человек шесть недель «короткой стопы», работы над голеностопом, бедром и растяжки изменили форму свода сильнее, чем в контрольной группе (Brijwasi и Borkar, 2023).
- Обзор 2024 года о «короткой стопе» не нашёл явных изменений в целом и нашёл улучшение одного показателя свода только в программах длиннее шести недель (Cheng и соавторы, 2024).
- Жёсткое плоскостопие, при котором стопа остаётся плоской даже на весу, связано со строением стопы, и упражнения не изменят её форму.
- Эти исследования измеряли форму свода, а не боль. При боли в пятке клинические рекомендации 2023 года дают растяжке подошвенной фасции и икр высший уровень, A, а силовым упражнениям уровень B.

### Как понять, гибкое у вас плоскостопие или жёсткое?

Гибкое у вас плоскостопие или жёсткое, можно понять за несколько секунд. Это важно, потому что исследование на этой странице проводилось при гибком плоскостопии, а форму жёсткой стопы упражнения не изменят. Обзор 2024 года объединял исследования плоскостопия в целом. Walkito не проверяет тип стопы, так что эту проверку вы делаете сами:

- Встаньте босиком и посмотрите на внутреннюю сторону стопы. При плоскостопии свод низкий или касается пола.
- Поднимите эту стопу от пола или встаньте на носки и посмотрите снова.
- Если свод вернулся, плоскостопие **гибкое**. Упражнения ниже как раз для него.
- Если свод остаётся плоским даже на весу, стопа **жёсткая**. Это вопрос строения стопы, и упражнения его не изменят. Отложите цель по удержанию свода и перед началом программы обратитесь к врачу.
- «Опущенным сводом» обычно называют то же плоскостопие. Но если свод одной стопы опустился **резко**, с одной стороны, уже во взрослом возрасте, обратитесь к врачу, прежде чем его тренировать, что бы ни показала проверка.

### Упражнения при плоскостопии и стартовые дозировки

Упражнения при плоскостопии в Walkito начинаются с собирания полотенца и подъёма большого пальца, а затем идут три версии «короткой стопы». Вокруг них: разведение пальцев, поворот стопы внутрь с лентой, стойка на одной ноге, отведение бедра и растяжка икр. Это стартовые дозировки Walkito, а не назначение. Делайте упражнения босиком. [Как написаны эти гайды](https://walkito.site/ru/o-proekte/).

«Короткая стопа» лежит в основе работы со сводом. Вы укорачиваете стопу, подтягивая подушечку стопы к пятке, так что свод поднимается, а пальцы не поджимаются. Именно «короткую стопу», укрепление бедра и растяжку проверяли в исследовании. Собирание полотенца, подъём большого пальца, разведение пальцев, поворот стопы внутрь и стойка на одной ноге добавлены Walkito.

Вы делаете одно упражнение для свода за раз, то, что соответствует вашему уровню. Walkito переводит вас на следующую ступень, когда два последних занятия с ним дались легко. Пока цель связана со сводом, в каждом занятии есть упражнение для свода, а остальные чередуются. Для некоторых упражнений нужны полотенце или резиновая лента. Walkito спрашивает, что у вас есть, и не включает то, для чего чего-то не хватает. Если какое-то упражнение поднимает боль до **6 из 10 или выше**, на сегодня остановитесь. На этой отметке Walkito завершает занятие.

- **Собирание полотенца** (3 подхода по 8, удержание 5 секунд, каждая стопа): Сядьте, расстелите полотенце на полу под стопой. Подтягивайте полотенце пальцами, пятка остаётся на полу. Это упражнение будит мелкие мышцы под сводом.
- **Подъём большого пальца** (3 подхода по 8, удержание 5 секунд, каждая стопа): Сядьте, стопы стоят на полу. Поднимите только большой палец и удерживайте. Остальные четыре пальца лежат на полу. Так большой палец учится двигаться отдельно, а это первый «включатель» свода.
- **Короткая стопа сидя** (3 подхода по 8, удержание 5 секунд, каждая стопа): Сядьте, стопа стоит на полу. Подтяните подушечку стопы к пятке, чтобы свод поднялся, и удерживайте. Не поджимайте пальцы. Поджатые пальцы самая частая ошибка в этом упражнении.
- **Короткая стопа стоя** (3 подхода по 8, удержание 5 секунд, обе стопы): Встаньте, вес на обеих стопах, и сделайте то же движение. Пальцы остаются ровными и длинными. Поднимается только свод. Мышца та же, что и сидя, но теперь она держит ваш вес.
- **Короткая стопа на одной ноге** (3 подхода по 10, удержание 5 секунд, каждая стопа): Встаньте на одну ногу и поднимите свод. Большой палец прижат к полу. Если он поднимается, свод «жульничает». При работе одной стопой видно, какая сторона слабее.
- **Разведение пальцев** (3 подхода по 10, каждая стопа): Разведите пальцы как можно шире и удерживайте. Пальцы, которые умеют расходиться, делят нагрузку со сводом. Поднимать их не нужно.
- **Поворот стопы внутрь с лентой** (3 подхода по 12, каждая стопа): Сядьте, наденьте резиновую ленту на стопу и поворачивайте стопу внутрь против её сопротивления. Двигается стопа, а не нога. Колено неподвижно. Walkito добавляет это упражнение только после шести занятий с «короткой стопой» стоя, чтобы сначала заработали собственные мышцы свода.
- **Стойка на одной ноге** (3 удержания по 20 секунд, каждая нога): Встаньте на одну ногу и смотрите в одну точку. Пусть стопа покачивается. Так и должно быть: эти покачивания и есть работа стопы по удержанию равновесия.
- **Отведение бедра** (3 подхода по 10, каждая нога): Встаньте с резиновой лентой и отведите одну ногу в сторону против её сопротивления. Давите пяткой, а не носком. Если бедро «проседает», нагрузка ложится на свод.
- **Растяжка икры и камбаловидной мышцы** (2 удержания по 30 секунд на каждую растяжку, каждая нога): Упритесь руками в стену. Задняя нога прямая, пятка на полу, таз подан вперёд: растяжение ощущается в икре. Затем согните колено задней ноги, пока растяжение не уйдёт ниже, к пятке. Это камбаловидная мышца, более глубокая мышца икры.

### Через сколько упражнения при плоскостопии меняют свод?

По имеющимся исследованиям, упражнения при плоскостопии меняли свод через шесть недель или больше и только при гибком плоскостопии. В исследовании с участием 52 человек с **гибким** плоскостопием шестинедельная программа из «короткой стопы», работы над голеностопом, укрепления бедра и растяжки изменила два показателя формы свода сильнее, чем в контрольной группе.

Данных о «короткой стопе» самой по себе меньше. Обзор 2024 года объединил исследования «короткой стопы» при плоскостопии в целом. В целом он не нашёл явной разницы с контрольными группами ни в форме свода, ни в положении стопы. Только программы длиннее шести недель уменьшили то, насколько свод проседает под весом, и авторы пишут, что нужны более крупные исследования. Так что закладывайте минимум шесть недель, а если делаете только «короткую стопу», то больше.

Это одна из причин, почему у плана Walkito нет даты окончания. Цель для свода, удержание 60 секунд, остаётся в плане, пока вы её не достигнете, сколько бы недель это ни заняло. Удержание свода проверяется тестом каждые 14 дней, пока не достигнута первая цель, затем каждые 28, так что видно, есть ли сдвиги. Исследования собраны на [странице с исследованиями](https://walkito.site/science/) (на английском).

Source: Brijwasi T, Borkar P. A comprehensive exercise program improves foot alignment in people with flexible flat foot: a randomised trial. Journal of Physiotherapy. 2023;69(1):42–46.
Source: Cheng J, Han D, Qu J, et al. Effects of short foot training on foot posture in patients with flatfeet: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Journal of Back and Musculoskeletal Rehabilitation. 2024;37(4):839–851.

### Помогают ли упражнения при плоскостопии от боли в своде?

Ни одно исследование на этой странице не показывает, что упражнения при плоскостопии уменьшают боль в своде, потому что ни одно из них её не измеряло. И исследование, и обзор измеряли форму свода. Они показывают, что свод можно тренировать. Но это не доказательство того, что те же упражнения облегчают ноющий свод.

Боль в пятке, а иногда и вдоль свода, может идти от подошвенной фасции, полосы ткани, которая тянется по подошве. Если у вас болит ближе к пятке, лучше опираться на клинические рекомендации 2023 года по боли в пятке. При боли в пятке под стопой они дают растяжке подошвенной фасции и икр высший уровень, **A**, а силовым упражнениям уровень **B**. Эти упражнения есть в гайде [упражнения при плантарном фасциите и боли в пятке](https://walkito.site/ru/bol-v-pyatke-uprazhneniya/).

Walkito может работать над обоим сразу, как над отдельными целями: «Лёгкие утра» для боли и удержание свода для свода. Как две цели делят неделю, описано на [странице о плане](https://walkito.site/program/) (на английском).

Source: Koc TA Jr, Bise CG, Neville C, et al. Heel Pain - Plantar Fasciitis: Revision 2023. Journal of Orthopaedic & Sports Physical Therapy. 2023;53(12):CPG1–CPG39.

### Что происходит, когда цель для свода достигнута?

Когда вы достигаете цели для свода, удержания 60 секунд, Walkito оставляет работу со сводом в плане с меньшей дозировкой. Цель переходит в поддержание, а её место занимает следующая. Достигнутая цель не значит, что работа со сводом прекращается.

Тесты тоже продолжаются, каждые 28 дней после первой достигнутой цели. Если удержание свода начнёт снижаться, вы увидите это по цифрам, а не будете гадать.

Если у вас болит ещё и пятка, для неё есть свои упражнения и своя цель: смотрите [упражнения при плантарном фасциите и боли в пятке](https://walkito.site/ru/bol-v-pyatke-uprazhneniya/). Ответы на вопросы о самом приложении есть в [FAQ](https://walkito.site/faq/) (на английском).

### Сначала обратитесь к врачу, если

- боль появилась после травмы или падения
- на ногу нельзя наступить или вы хромаете
- боль сопровождается онемением, покалыванием, жжением, отёком или ощущением жара
- пятка покраснела, у вас температура или общее недомогание
- боль будит вас ночью
- боль острая или усиливается, хотя вы снизили нагрузку
- больно сжимать пятку с боков или боль нарастает во время пробежек после того, как вы увеличили объём бега: и то и другое может быть признаком стрессового перелома
- у вас диабет, сниженная чувствительность стоп или плохое кровообращение
- болят обе пятки, а другие суставы опухают или скованы
- за несколько недель упражнений и сниженной нагрузки лучше не стало
- свод одной стопы резко опустился уже во взрослом возрасте
- свод остаётся плоским, когда стопа на весу

### Всё это как план
